inputs.source: Published HR policy documents, HR-maintained, read only to the agent

instructions.note: The boundary against giving legal advice is enforced only by a prompt instruction ('Do not give legal advice'); no structural check prevents the model from answering a legally-flavored question it frames as policy explanation.

controls.name: Read-only credential scoped to the published policy index
Chat reply routed only to the authenticated requester's own session
Network-layer egress denial, no outbound network access, verified by pen test
Two-person review required before publishing to the policy index
SSO authentication of the employee chat session
Model version pinned; upgrade requires a change ticket
System prompt restricts scope to published HR policy Q&A and forbids legal advice
controls.decay_rationale: A more capable or adversarially prompted model may rationalize exceptions to the instruction, for example providing legal interpretation framed as policy explanation.

controls.name: Change-ticket and security review gate before widening the policy_search credential scope

findings.title: Internal published HR policy content reaches the employee through the chat-reply egress sink

attack_path.note: HR-maintained published policy content, internal sensitivity
Agent reads the policy index with a scoped, read-only credential
Quoted policy content is sent back to the employee's chat session (egress, internal data)

forecast.watch_signal: The policy_search credential scope widens beyond published policies (for example to unpublished or confidential HR content), or the chat-reply recipient binding is changed to allow routing replies to a destination other than the requester's own session.

evidence.observation: "The policy index holds only published policies. Data sensitivity is internal... The agent's credential is read only and scoped to the policy index."
"Replies go only to the authenticated requester's chat session."

recommendations.action: Require a change ticket and security review before widening the policy_search credential scope beyond currently published policies, and alert if policy_search begins returning content marked confidential or restricted.

findings.title: No attributable, tamper-evident record of employee Q&A exchanges

forecast.watch_signal: Autonomy level raised to A4_fully_autonomous, or max_unattended_steps/max_runtime_minutes limits removed or relaxed.

evidence.observation: No logging, audit, or provenance requirement is specified for replies or searches.
The only declared tool is policy_search.search; no logging tool or audit mechanism is declared.
Runtime notes describe credential scope, egress denial, and autonomy, but make no statement about logging or audit records of agent actions.

recommendations.action: Implement tamper-evident logging of each Q&A exchange (employee identity from SSO, question, retrieved policy citation, reply text, timestamp), retained for audit and dispute resolution.

stride_coverage.rationale: The agent is an internal backend service invoked only through the organization's SSO-authenticated chat client; there is no external protocol peer or agent identity in this design that could be spoofed.
No artifact describes change control, versioning, or integrity protection for the system prompt or agent configuration beyond the stated model-version pinning process.
No artifact states a query rate limit, concurrency cap, or resource quota for policy_search invocations or the chat endpoint.
No artifact describes access controls on the policy index for readers other than the agent's scoped credential, such as direct database or admin access.
No artifact describes capacity limits or availability protections for the policy index backing the search tool.
No artifact describes transport integrity protections such as TLS for the chat channel carrying employee questions to the agent.
No artifact describes whether employee questions, which may contain personal context, are logged or retained outside the agent's immediate processing.
No artifact states a limit on the number or frequency of questions a single employee session may submit.
No artifact describes integrity protection for reply content in transit between the agent and the employee's chat client.

Each employee question produces exactly one bounded chat reply with no bulk-send or repeat-trigger mechanism, so this flow cannot itself be used to exhaust resources beyond the per-question volume already assessed at the process level.

rating.rationale: Both findings stem from internal-source data (published HR policy content and the authenticated employee's own question), not from any untrusted source; the design has no web, email, or third-party tool input. f.policy_disclosure_egress is inherently moderate (internal data reaching an egress sink) but its residual drops to low because the read credential is scoped to the published policy index only and the chat reply is structurally bound to the requester's own authenticated session, leaving no path today for the disclosed content to reach an unintended recipient or a higher-sensitivity source. f.no_audit_log stays at moderate for both inherent and residual because no control in the design restores an attributable, tamper-evident record of what the agent told employees. The forecast rises to high under two conditions: if data_scope_expansion or control_removal widens the policy_search credential beyond published policies, the egress sink could carry confidential or restricted content instead of internal content, removing the containment that currently holds f.policy_disclosure_egress at low; and if autonomy_increase removes the single-turn, bounded-step design, the missing audit trail becomes a more severe gap under the rubric's autonomy modifier. The single control whose decay moves the forecast most is c.credential_scope (the read-only, policy-index-scoped credential): it is the only structural control standing between today's internal-only disclosure and a confidential or restricted-data disclosure path.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts, not observed runtime behavior; no logs, traces, or live testing were reviewed.
No MCP or other protocol configuration was provided; policy_search.search is treated as a local tool call with no separate protocol-level trust assessment.

Autonomy limits (max_unattended_steps, max_runtime_minutes) are inferred from the single-turn, request/response architecture described in the artifacts; no explicit numeric limits were stated, so confidence on the autonomy modifier is medium.

Query volume, rate limiting, and transport-layer integrity protections for the chat channel and policy index are not described in the artifacts and were marked not_assessed rather than assumed safe or unsafe.
